_note: V5.3 a, the plant-closure rule (docs/design/v5.3-ab.md 3.2, src/sim/closures.gd). STAND-INS written by Systems so the rule can be measured; Content authors the numbers (the spec's section 10), as data, never per firm. window_months: the months over which a major's output fall is measured. fall: the fraction of its output a major must lose over the window for its sector to announce a closure. cut: the share of the picked firm's live share, so of its jobs, a landed closure removes (a plant, not the firm). cooldown_months: the months after a closure ends before the same SECTOR may announce again (at least window + the answer's months, so a landed closure's own cut never re-announces). bloc_offset: what a landed closure of reference_jobs moves; a plant moves it in proportion to its jobs. V5.3 majors (the parent's ruling): the rule fires per sector, one major picked by its share of the sector's jobs, so adding real majors does not change the calibrated rate; per major, FRA went from 14 closures a decade to 39. reference_jobs is about the mean plant at the real majors' shares (tools/closure_rate_probe.gd), so the mean closure moves #251's -0.02.
